evidence.locator: Framework landing page: “was agreed to and released ... on 21 June 2024.”
Page date 22/10/2026, paragraphs 8–18: commitment language and reference to the existing framework; no new requirements announced.

reason: A primary-source recheck of the Department of Finance framework landing page explicitly dates agreement and release to 21 June 2024. The statement page dated 22 October 2026 calls that existing framework a key step and adds no new requirement. Correct the public event date and preserve the earlier edition as historical record.
summary: Corrected the event date for the Australian national framework for assurance of AI in government. The official landing page says the framework was agreed and released on 21 June 2024; the previously recorded 8 October 2026 date mistook a current page date for the original policy event. The 22 October 2026 ministerial statement reaffirms commitment to safe and responsible government AI and refers to the existing framework, but does not announce a new framework release.

evidence.locator: 14 October 2026 press release, opening paragraph and sectoral performance: revised Q2 and Q3 estimates.
Key Highlights and About Advance GDP Estimates: revised comparison, July–August basis and revision caveat.

reason: Direct inspection of the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry release and Singapore Department of Statistics page showed the updated Q2 comparison and the advance-estimate method. The older July values were valid at publication but are superseded by the later revision; they should not be used as October's current baseline. None of these aggregate figures isolates AI's causal contribution.
summary: Corrected the prior Q2 GDP comparator in the MAS AI-cycle review. MAS's July statement cited preliminary Q2 2026 growth of 5.7% y/y and 1.1% q/q seasonally adjusted. The 14 October MTI/SingStat advance Q3 release revises Q2 to 6.2% y/y and 1.5% q/q, and reports Q3 at 5.4% and 1.1%, respectively. The Q3 estimate is preliminary and subject to revision.
